title: Jeremiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 11.

questions.question: Who received the word from the LORD in Jeremiah 11?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah is the one who received the word from the LORD as stated in Jeremiah 11:1.

questions.question: To whom was Jeremiah commanded to speak the words of the covenant?
options: Men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was told to speak unto the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 11:2.

questions.question: What is the consequence for the man who does not obey the words of the covenant?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:3 states that cursed is the man that obeyeth not the words of the covenant.

questions.question: From which land did God bring the fathers of Judah and Israel out?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:4 mentions that God brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt.

questions.question: What did God promise to give to the fathers as an oath in Jeremiah 11?
options: A land flowing with milk and honey
questions.correctAnswer: A land flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:5 states the oath to give them a land flowing with milk and honey.

questions.question: What was Jeremiah told to proclaim in the cities of Judah and streets of Jerusalem?
options: Hear ye the words of this covenant, and do them
questions.correctAnswer: Hear ye the words of this covenant, and do them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:6 commands Jeremiah to proclaim the words of the covenant and to do them.

questions.question: How did God repeatedly protest to the fathers from the day He brought them out of Egypt?
options: Rising early and protesting, saying, Obey my voice
questions.correctAnswer: Rising early and protesting, saying, Obey my voice
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:7 describes how God earnestly protested by rising early and protesting.

questions.question: True or False: The people obeyed God’s voice and inclined their ear to Him.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:8 says they obeyed not nor inclined their ear but walked in their evil heart's imagination.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was commanded to speak only in Jerusalem about the covenant.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:6 instructs him to proclaim in the cities of Judah and streets of Jerusalem, not just in Jerusalem alone.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He would bring upon those who did not obey the covenant?
options: All the words of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: All the words of the covenant
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:8 states God will bring upon them all the words of the covenant because they did not obey.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 11, what comes first: the LORD commanding Jeremiah to proclaim the words of the covenant or the LORD protesting to the fathers to obey His voice?
options: LORD commanding Jeremiah to proclaim the words
LORD protesting to the fathers to obey His voice
questions.correctAnswer: LORD commanding Jeremiah to proclaim the words
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:6 records the LORD commanding Jeremiah to proclaim first, followed by His protest to the fathers in 11:7.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah responded to God's oath by saying, 'So be it, O LORD.'
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:5 shows Jeremiah answering, 'So be it, O LORD.' after God’s promise.

questions.question: What did God command the fathers to do from the day He brought them out of Egypt?
options: Obey His voice and do all He commanded
questions.correctAnswer: Obey His voice and do all He commanded
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:4 commands obedience to God’s voice and all His commands given since Egypt.

questions.question: Who were the intended recipients of Jeremiah's message about the covenant?
options: Men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: Men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:2 clearly states Jeremiah was to speak to the men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Judah walked according to the imagination of their evil heart.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:8 affirms they walked every one in the imagination of their evil heart.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 11:9, what did the LORD reveal about the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
options: A conspiracy is found among them
They have built new altars to the LORD
They have repented and returned to God
questions.correctAnswer: A conspiracy is found among them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:9 states that the LORD told Jeremiah a conspiracy was found among the men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, indicating their secret rebellion against God's covenant.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:10 say the people of Judah and Israel have done that breaks God's covenant?
options: They went after other gods to serve them
They built altars to the LORD alone
questions.correctAnswer: They went after other gods to serve them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:10 explains that both houses of Israel and Judah turned back to the sins of their forefathers by refusing to hear God's words and serving other gods, thus breaking His covenant.

questions.question: What consequence does the LORD declare in Jeremiah 11:11 for those who break His covenant?
options: He will bring evil upon them from which they cannot escape
He will forgive them if they repent
He will bless them with peace
He will send prophets to guide them
questions.correctAnswer: He will bring evil upon them from which they cannot escape
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:11 states that God will bring unavoidable evil upon those who break His covenant, and He will not hear their cries even if they call upon Him.

questions.question: Based on Jeremiah 11:12, what will the cities of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem do in their time of trouble, and what will be the outcome?
options: They will cry to the gods they offer incense to, but these gods will not save them
They will cry unto the LORD and be delivered
They will fight their enemies and win
They will repent and be restored immediately
questions.correctAnswer: They will cry to the gods they offer incense to, but these gods will not save them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:12 explains that in their time of trouble, the people will cry to the false gods they worship, but these gods will not save them, showing the futility of idolatry.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:13 reveal about the extent of idolatry in Judah and Jerusalem?
options: The number of gods and altars matched the number of cities and streets
Only a few altars were set up for Baal
They worshipped only one God sincerely
questions.correctAnswer: The number of gods and altars matched the number of cities and streets
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:13 states that according to the number of cities in Judah and streets in Jerusalem, numerous gods and altars to Baal were set up, illustrating widespread idolatry.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 11:14 instruct Jeremiah regarding prayer for the people, and why?
options: Do not pray for them because God will not hear them in their trouble
Pray for forgiveness on their behalf
questions.correctAnswer: Do not pray for them because God will not hear them in their trouble
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:14 commands Jeremiah not to pray or cry out for the people because God will not hear them when they cry to Him in their trouble due to their persistent disobedience.

questions.question: What question does God ask in Jeremiah 11:15 about 'my beloved' and what does it imply about their behavior?
options: What hath my beloved to do in mine house, seeing she hath wrought lewdness with many?
Why does my beloved worship me alone?
Who is my beloved that obeys my commands?
Where is my beloved hiding from me?
questions.correctAnswer: What hath my beloved to do in mine house, seeing she hath wrought lewdness with many?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:15 questions why God's beloved (Israel) is in His house when she has committed lewdness with many, symbolizing unfaithfulness and evil behavior.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 11:16, how does the LORD describe Israel, and what has happened to her?
options: A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit, but fire has been kindled and branches broken
A barren fig tree without fruit
A mighty cedar untouched by fire
questions.correctAnswer: A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit, but fire has been kindled and branches broken
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:16 portrays Israel as a flourishing olive tree, but turmoil has caused fire to be kindled and branches to be broken, symbolizing judgment on her unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:17 say is the reason for the evil pronounced against Israel and Judah?
options: They provoked God to anger by offering incense to Baal
They built new altars to the LORD
They repented and turned back to God
questions.correctAnswer: They provoked God to anger by offering incense to Baal
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:17 declares that the evil pronounced against the houses of Israel and Judah is due to their provocation of God’s anger through idol worship, specifically offering incense to Baal.

questions.question: What knowledge did the LORD give Jeremiah according to Jeremiah 11:18?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:18 states that the LORD gave Jeremiah knowledge of the conspiracy against him and showed him the doings of the people, demonstrating divine revelation.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 11:19, how does Jeremiah describe himself in relation to the devices devised against him?
options: Like a lamb or an ox brought to the slaughter, unaware of the conspiracy
Like a mighty warrior ready for battle
Like a tree with strong roots
Like a wise judge discerning truth
questions.correctAnswer: Like a lamb or an ox brought to the slaughter, unaware of the conspiracy
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:19 compares Jeremiah to a lamb or ox unaware of the plans to destroy him, indicating his innocence and vulnerability to the conspirators.

questions.question: What plea does Jeremiah make to the LORD in Jeremiah 11:20 regarding his enemies?
options: Let me see Your vengeance on them, for I have revealed my cause to You
questions.correctAnswer: Let me see Your vengeance on them, for I have revealed my cause to You
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 11:20, Jeremiah asks the LORD, the righteous judge, to bring vengeance on those who plot against him, acknowledging that he has shared his cause before God.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 11:21, what threat do the men of Anathoth make against Jeremiah?
options: They threaten to kill him if he prophesies in the LORD's name
They ask him to be their leader
They invite him to their homes
questions.correctAnswer: They threaten to kill him if he prophesies in the LORD's name
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:21 reveals that the men of Anathoth threaten Jeremiah’s life, warning him not to prophesy in the LORD’s name or he will be killed by their hand.

questions.question: What punishment does God declare for the men of Anathoth in Jeremiah 11:22?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:22 states that God will punish the men of Anathoth by causing young men to die by the sword and their children by famine, showing divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 11:23, what will happen to the men of Anathoth in the year of their visitation?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:23 proclaims there will be no remnant of the men of Anathoth after God's visitation, indicating complete destruction rather than survival.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 11.

questions.question: What is the reason the LORD pronounces evil against the house of Israel and Judah in Jeremiah 11:17?
options: They worshipped Baal and provoked God's anger
They built many altars to the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They worshipped Baal and provoked God's anger
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:17 states that the LORD pronounces evil against them for provoking Him to anger by offering incense to Baal.

questions.question: In Jeremiah 11:18, what did the LORD give Jeremiah knowledge of?
options: The designs of the men of Judah against him
The building of a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: The designs of the men of Judah against him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:18 explains that the LORD gave Jeremiah knowledge of the conspiracies devised by the men of Judah and showed him their doings.

questions.question: Jeremiah 11:19 uses the simile 'like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter.' What does this imagery primarily indicate about Jeremiah's situation?
options: He is innocent yet unaware of the plots against him
He is physically strong and ready to fight
He is victorious over his enemies
questions.correctAnswer: He is innocent yet unaware of the plots against him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:19 portrays Jeremiah as innocent and unaware of the conspiracies against him, similar to a lamb or ox unaware of its impending slaughter.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah ask the LORD to do in Jeremiah 11:20?
options: To show vengeance on his enemies
To bless the city of Jerusalem
To grant him a long life
questions.correctAnswer: To show vengeance on his enemies
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 11:20, Jeremiah prays for the LORD to execute righteous judgment and vengeance on those who conspire against him.

questions.question: Who are the men of Anathoth mentioned in Jeremiah 11:21?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:21 identifies the men of Anathoth as those who seek Jeremiah's life and threaten him for prophesying in the name of the LORD.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 11:22, how will the LORD punish the men of Anathoth?
options: The young men by the sword and their children by famine
They will be exiled to Babylon
They will be blessed with peace
questions.correctAnswer: The young men by the sword and their children by famine
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:22 states that the LORD will punish the men of Anathoth with death by sword for the young men and famine for their sons and daughters.

questions.question: What is the final outcome for the men of Anathoth as declared in Jeremiah 11:23?
options: There shall be no remnant of them
They will be redeemed by God
They will build a new temple
questions.correctAnswer: There shall be no remnant of them
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:23 declares that there will be no survivors among the men of Anathoth because of the evil God will bring upon them.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Jeremiah 11:19 where Jeremiah compares himself to a lamb or ox brought to slaughter?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:19 uses a simile by comparing Jeremiah to a lamb or ox that is brought to slaughter using the word 'like'.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'conspiracy' in Jeremiah 11:9 most closely means what?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 11:9, the Hebrew word for 'conspiracy' refers to a secret plan or plot against Jeremiah and God's purposes.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God’s covenant being broken and resulting judgment as seen in Jeremiah 11?
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 28 outlines blessings for obedience and curses for breaking the covenant, a theme central to Jeremiah 11's message.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 11:11-12 foreshadow the Babylonian exile?
options: By declaring inescapable evil and false gods unable to save in times of trouble
By describing the building of a new temple
By announcing the end of sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: By declaring inescapable evil and false gods unable to save in times of trouble
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:11-12 forewarn of judgment from which there is no escape and the inability of idols to save, foreshadowing the Babylonian exile’s suffering.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse reflects the theme of righteous judgment and the testing of hearts found in Jeremiah 11:20?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 4:12 speaks about the word of God judging thoughts and intents of the heart, paralleling Jeremiah 11:20’s mention of God judging reins and hearts.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:16's description of Judah as 'a green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit' symbolize?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:16 uses the olive tree metaphor to symbolize Judah’s favored status before God’s judgment kindled fire upon it.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah was aware from the beginning of the devices the men of Judah had devised against him as stated in Jeremiah 11:19.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:19 states he 'knew not' that the conspirators had devised devices against him, indicating his initial unawareness.

questions.question: True or False: Jeremiah 11:14 instructs Jeremiah to pray fervently for the people when they cry out in trouble.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:14 commands Jeremiah not to pray for the people, for God will not hear them in their time of trouble.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:3 declare about those who do not obey the covenant?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:3 states, 'Cursed be the man that obeyeth not the words of this covenant,' indicating the consequence of disobedience to God's commands.

questions.question: What is the consequence of disobeying the covenant according to Jeremiah 11:11?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:11 reveals God's judgment, stating, 'I will bring evil upon them, which they shall not be able to escape.' This underscores the seriousness of disobedience.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 11:10, what had the house of Israel and the house of Judah done?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:10 states, 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with their fathers,' indicating their rebellion against God.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'iron furnace' in Jeremiah 11:4 symbolize?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:4 references the 'iron furnace,' symbolizing the severe oppression and slavery the Israelites endured in Egypt, from which God delivered them.

questions.question: What does God call the people of Judah in Jeremiah 11:16?
questions.explanation: In Jeremiah 11:16, God refers to Judah as 'A green olive tree, fair, and of goodly fruit,' indicating their initial beauty and potential before judgment.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:14 instruct regarding prayer for the people?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:14 states, 'Therefore pray not thou for this people,' indicating God's rejection of their pleas due to their persistent sin.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:8 say about the people's response to God's commands?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:8 clearly states, 'Yet they obeyed not, nor inclined their ear,' showing their refusal to listen to God's instructions.

questions.question: What does the term 'conspiracy' in Jeremiah 11:9 refer to?
options: A secret plan to follow God
A plan to unite the people
A conspiracy among the men of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: A conspiracy among the men of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:9 mentions, 'A conspiracy is found among the men of Judah,' indicating their collusion against God's will.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:12 suggest will happen when the people cry to their gods?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:12 states, 'but they shall not save them at all in the time of their trouble,' indicating that their false gods will fail to deliver them.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 11:19 describe Jeremiah's realization of the people's plans against him?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:19 describes Jeremiah as 'like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter; and I knew not that they had devised devices against me,' indicating his initial ignorance of their intentions.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 11:21 reveal about the men of Anathoth?
options: They are in alliance with the Babylonians
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:21 states that the men of Anathoth sought Jeremiah's life, showing the extreme opposition he faced for his prophecies.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah' in Jeremiah 11:17 indicate?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:17 indicates that the 'evil of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah' provoked God to anger, highlighting their sinful behavior.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 4 and 5 convey about obedience to God's commands?
options: Obedience is only for the leaders
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 5 emphasize that obedience to God's commands establishes a covenant relationship and brings blessings, as seen in verse 5.

questions.question: What combined insight does Jeremiah 11:8 and 10 provide about the people's behavior?
options: They were confused about God's will
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:8 and 10 together show that the people not only disobeyed God's commands but also returned to the iniquities of their forefathers, indicating a pattern of rebellion.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God does not punish disobedience. What does Jeremiah 11:11-12 actually teach?
options: God will not punish His people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 11:11-12 clearly indicates that God will bring punishment upon those who disobey His covenant, demonstrating that He does not overlook sin.
